utterances.text: Just my feeling at the time, trying to get -- just react off body language and facial expression. And, remember, I do speak Croatian, so I was getting the full force of what he was saying and the sentences, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I appreciate that. My question to you was about your knowledge of his authority, and I think you had already agreed with me that you're not actually in a position to deal with that topic.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, just to conclude and to put this into context, during the course of the interview, you asked him if he would go to the village to see for himself. Remember?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: He told you that he would --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: -- if he had sometime after the arrival of the president --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: -- which was to take place that day on the 26th.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Did you go back to his office to see him, to see if he had time that day?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I can't remember whether he said -- did he say that he -- I seem to remember him suggesting that the president was coming, which meant that he couldn't go back. Maybe I've not remembered correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: No, I don't think you have. I'm going to try and assist you with the words that were used. You say to him: "Would the General be prepared to go with us to the village to see this for himself?"

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: His answer is: "Here, this afternoon, if I have sometime after the president's arrival, definitely." And my question to you was simply, did you go back to his offices to check?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And, in fact, you never went back to Grubori, I think it's right in saying that, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And you left for Knin that night?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm, for Split.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Yeah. So you left Knin, and you ended up going to Zagreb, in fact, that night?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, you asked him twice during the interview if he would personally undertake an investigation. Did you ever know or come to know subsequently that, in fact, Mr. Cermak did not have the right or ability to conduct an investigation? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Mr. Lyntton, thank you very much. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Higgins. Before we have a break, Mr. Lyntton, one question: Did you ever come to know about other business activities of Mr. Cermak than the one you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you ever intend to make another production on the person or activities of Mr. Cermak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Higgins, where I earlier said that you did not limit your question, I was wrong, because you said "during your research ..." At the same time, your question about knowledge of Mr. Lyntton was rather broad. You said: "Did you ever come to know ..." The reason why I asked him whether he ever came to know anything else about the commercial or business activities of Mr. Cermak was, for myself, to form a further opinion on whether this was a selective approach or whether it was an answer you would expect from a witness who is asked this question. About the tone, I'm not going to change that. But about the way you introduced that matter, there was some limitation that I made a mistake there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I hope you accept my apology about the tone. I did try to tone it down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I did not seek at this moment an apology for it. I just want to let you know that my observation was not in every respect correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have a break, and we'll resume at 25 minutes to 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, are you ready --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to cross-examine Mr. Lyntton? Mr. Kuzmanovic is Defence counsel for Mr. Markac. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You're biographical information in your statement, which is P870, talks about you spending six months in Sarajevo and six months in Pale. What did you do in your six months in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the UNHCR liaison officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And as that liaison officer, what was your function?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was to ensure that the -- the Bosnian government people in Sarajevo got their fuel convoys and their humanitarian aid food through the check-points, and then I would go around to the warehouses and check that the food -- the humanitarian aid was being distributed properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you under fire at that point at any time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it a daily occurrence that you would be under fire?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not directly. But there were -- at the time that I arrived, there were on average 1.000 to 1.300 shells landing in Sarajevo and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Per day?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, per day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And then you had spent six months in Pale?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And what did you do there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the UNMO, Pale; United Nations Military Observer, Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And what was your function as the United Nations Military Observer in Pale?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was to facilitate communications between the Bosnian Serb headquarters and the General Rose's UNPROFOR headquarters down in Sarajevo through satellite telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So you worked for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, it is even difficult to get something in between of the answer and your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This has consequences for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: As usual, I will try to calm down after your admonition, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, for the record, we could ask Mr. Lyntton to repeat what his function was during his six months in Pale. You were an --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: UNMO, United Nations Military Observer. There were -- there was an office. It was the only office, bar one, on Bosnian Serb territory where there were UNMOs, and we facilitated the communications between the Bosnian Serb military and civilian headquarters and the UNPROFOR headquarters down in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And said that you worked for General Rose?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I was -- well, not directly for him but -- because the UNMOs were commanded by a chief UNMO in Zagreb. But, yes, I was communicating with HQ UNPROFOR which was in Sarajevo, which was commanded by General Rose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And then with whom did you communicate on the Bosnian Serb military and civilian side?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mainly by fax and telephone, with liaison officers, because there was a satellite telephone in our office in Pale. So all the communications would come via local telephone line, and then we would satellite fax them down to Sarajevo. That was kind of the main job.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you said you had learned Croatian. Were you speaking Serbian or -- when you were in Pale with --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was speaking Serbo-Croatian or Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned that -- the British Army sent me on a three-month course, it was called a colloquial speaker course, and that was prior it my posting as an UNHCR LO in Sarajevo, and because I also spoke Russian. I mean, that's why I was sent on the course because I spoke Russian, and they wanted Russian speakers to learn Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: When you were in Croatian, did you need an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: When you went on the trip to Knin, did you need an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Except for obviously the interview with General Cermak, and because -- and I decided to that because I just felt it was an important interview, and my understanding would have been about 70 , 80 per cent. So, obviously, for that kind of interview, I just had the UN local interpreter come with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, when you were on your way for the first time up to the Plavno valley on the 25th, who was with you in your vehicle?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: My British cameraman who also worked for UN TV, and my assistant producer who was from the Czech Republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that who Sasa was?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did either your cameraman or the Sasa speak Croatian?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Czech guy, Sasa, may have spoken a few words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. My apologies to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 7 of your statement, sir, do you have the statement in front of you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The second sentence of that statement -- or the third sentence says: "The information we received was that a local chief of police was going around to the villages to assure local Serbs that it was safe to stay. We wanted to record one of these meetings." From whom did you get the information that you refer to in paragraph 7 that a local police chief was going around to the villages?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Flynn.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And did you ever get the name of who that local police chief was?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever attempt to contact that person?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In -- in the sense that when I got the interview with General Cermak, I assumed that perhaps the police chief would be --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Hang on, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It's my fault. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Go ahead, sir.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the sense that I assumed that maybe I would find the police chief with -- in the same building as General Cermak or some -- someone that -- someone that could have given me an interview who was, in fact, the person going round to those villages. In other words, if I couldn't speak to a person on the ground, I hoped that I would be able to speak to someone when I got back to Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And to this day, you haven't determined who that local police chief was?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Or from what city or municipality that police chief was?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, because they'd all just arrived. The Croatians had just arrived, so, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the information that you got regarding the local chief of police was from Mr. Flynn?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 9 of your statement, you talk about stopping at a farm house along the way to the Plavno area. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you talk about the old couple that you interviewed, and one of the things that you say in your statement at the bottom of page 2, going into page 3, you say: "The couple told us -- said it was Ustasha that were responsible for this treatment. I can't say if it was Croat police or military. The couple said the persons responsible were Croats in uniform with the Croatian emblem on their uniform. The incident relates to us had happened two or three days earlier. The interview of the elderly couple was videotaped." Now, I would like you to refer --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could pull up just the transcript of P871, which is the transcript from the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And I have a copy for you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And if I could ask the assistance of the usher, and if the Court would like, I have copies forever the Court, too, if the Court would like a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wasn't this annexed to the motion --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was annexed to the 92 ter, Your Honours. I just wanted to make sure that if you wanted an extra copy, I had it available.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lyntton, it is -- it is six pages long, and you can feel free -- I'm going to ask you some questions about this transcript, so I'd like to you take a look at and page through it and read it before I ask you some questions about it, in fairness to you. And just let me know when you're done.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with this --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- from Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There is nothing in this transcript that says Ustasha was responsible for this treatment. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So you put in your statement that they said it was Ustasha, but the persons that you interviewed never said that. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's not in the transcript. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. But this was just an interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the interview that you produced for us or that was produced to us never said anything about Ustasha being responsible for this --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the interview. Although, to be honest, I could be wrong about this. I just remember -- and I don't know. There's a lot of raw footage. So either I remember from the footage or, you know, the actual interview, or it was just in conversation; but, I mean, those words were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There's nothing in the transcript, however, that reflected that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct? And you know that Ustasha is considered to be a derogatory term for Croatians, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you also say or there's nothing in the transcript here that says that the couple said the persons were -- who were responsible were Croats in uniform with Croatian emblem on their uniform. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. Ask that again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly. Nothing in the transcript at least in the interview says the persons responsible were Croats in uniform with the Croatian emblem on their uniform. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, except I guess he says special forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you don't know what special forces are, do you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can imagine what Croatian special forces are. I do know what British special forces are. I can only imagine that Croatian was similar at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: But you don't know that specifically, do you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And didn't see them, correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: During the course of the interview of this couple, and I believe during direct examination, you had stated that you had heard one gunshot, and I'll refer to page 6, line 7 of the transcript. If you look in this particular transcript, P871, at line 28, there's a notation that there was an explosion in the distance. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It was not a gunshot?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been a gunshot. If you listen to the tape, it's -- it is debatable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you don't know for sure --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: -- one way or the other?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you don't know if that was an unexploded ordnance or whether it was a mine or whether it was a shell or what it was?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to refer you to paragraph 13 of your statement. You had described in your direct examination huge plumes of smoke in the distance, and you stated you later learned that the plumes of smoke were coming from the village of Grubori, and you said the distance was about three kilometres across the valley. You were at this spot where you saw the smoke for about 45 minutes. What was the purpose of you being in that particular spot at that time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first village?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose was to film a positive UN almost propaganda-style film about Serbs and Croats coming together, and I was told that the meeting would go take place at 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you waited there and there was no meeting?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No Croatian authority person showed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There was also some indication that UNPROFOR had called this meeting, was it not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think perhaps -- I don't know the answer, but perhaps -- I mean, I presume that UNPROFOR had tried to organise these meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's turn to 65 ter 3770, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And if this is already an exhibit, I did not write the exhibit number down, so I apologise. It's another -- just the transcript to this particular -- it's a video, but it's just the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry. Should I be looking at something now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah. Hopefully, it will pop up on your screen shortly. This is it, the transcript of your 25th August interview, and you're talking with a gentleman by the name of Vlado Savic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And UK 1, I presume, is the questioner, correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And UK 2 is the person responding to the questions?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And if you see under the UK 2, as a prelude to what I was asking you about before, this gentleman says, toward the bottom, right about the middle of page: "I don't know. The Croatian army came through. They just told me, 'Old man, sit here, don't leave the house, and nobody will touch you.' And that is how it was until today." And then you asked the question: "The Croatian army came through? I presuming you're the questioner, correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the answer is: "The Croatian army came through. They didn't touch anything. They just said, 'Stay at home and don't go out because they're shooting, you know.'" And later, on the next page, you ask: "What to expect today? Why is there there meeting today?" And the answer: "Well, we can expect a normalization of life in this town of Plavno. I think that life will normalize, that people who want to ..." And then you interject and say: "Just a minute. Today ... and can you say today there was a meeting with UNPROFOR and the police chief and the mayor of the Croatian government will come ... that's what you have to say." Now, you're telling the person what to say there, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you're telling the person that there is a meeting with UNPROFOR, the police chief, and the mayor of the Croatian government. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you get that information?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was supposed to be -- I mean, Flynn -- Flynn basically told me that there was going to be a meeting with, as I say, the -- when I say the mayor of the Croatian government, that's -- I mean, I thought it was the mayor of that town, the police chief, and UNPROFOR. So I don't know why I said the mayor of the Croatian government. Maybe, maybe I assumed at the time that the new mayor of Knin was sort of coming to, you know, say hello to these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That is sheer speculation though, right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, not only was there no appearance by what you term here "the police chief and the mayor," but there was no UNPROFOR either, right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So no one came.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And it wasn't just that someone --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except the UN humanitarian officer, and he was assuming -- the reason we went was because he was assuming that all this was going to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. And as a matter of fact, the person to whom you say, "today ... can you say today there was a meeting with UNPROFOR," basically repeats what you say in the next line: "Today UNPROFOR was here." And, in fact, UNPROFOR was not there.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What -- the translation would be "dana nje sastanak" [phoen]. I was trying to get him to say, because he had already said it and everyone -- we had already had a conversation about this. And when you film an interview, the bane, the problem of any journalist's life, especially when you're dealing with foreign languages, is you need complete sentences. So I need the guy to say -- if he is telling me -- there is no point in saying "meeting here today." I need him to say, "there is a meeting," because that is what -- that's what I'm going to put in my film. I get the old man saying, "Today, there's going to a meeting."

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So what you're doing here is you're not asking questions and he's not giving answers. You're telling him what to answer, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right there, that moment, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, you're doing it throughout most of this interview. If you look on page four at the bottom of page 3, you say: "No, no, from the beginning, from the beginning. What meeting was there this morning and who to except later?" And then the gentleman answers: "There was a meeting with the peacekeeping forces; that is to say, with UNPROFOR." But there was no meeting with UNPROFOR, was there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. And he continues: "And we expect the mayor and other Croatian authorities who are in Knin. But in Plavno today, there was nobody." And other than you, that is an accurate statement: In Plavno, there was nobody from UNPROFOR, there was no mayor, and there were no Croatian authorities. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. I mean, what perhaps is worth explaining is that you talk to people when you arrive in a place, and the old man - and, again, I can't remember - but he probably said something like, "Yeah. We're having a meeting today, "because that is it what he had been told. So all I am trying to do -- the reason it probably looks a little bit odd is I'm just trying to get someone from the village saying, "there's a meeting today," in a full sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: But you're telling him -- you're telling him that in the way you want him to say it, not in the way he was actually was saying it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I need him to say a full sentence for the piece. I mean, any interview needs to use full sentences. So, yes, I'm telling him the sentence. He may have said another -- he may have said it a different way. But I need, for my piece, I need the full sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if we look at page 6 of this same transcript in the middle, just above UK 1, the gentleman says: "I thought this was an integral part of Croatia and that it would remain Croatian because the superpowers were so inclined." And then you say: "Just a minute, just a minute. You must start with Serbian Krajina, they came, the Serbian army or Serbian Krajina. I don't know how you're going to say it, but you can start with Serbian Krajina came." I mean, you're basically asking him to answer the question the way you want it answered.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, because I can't use what he is saying in the way saying it. It is going to be nonsense when I cut it together.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you say later again: "Just a minute, just a minute. When Serbian Krajina started, that's how have you to start your sentence."

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because you have got to remember I didn't speak perfect Bosnian. So I'm trying to get those complete sentences, two or three sentences, for my piece that are going to say, you know, "today, there is a meeting." I just need someone from the village to say that for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: On page 8 of this same document --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we can go to page eight.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry. I don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Page 8 of 65 ter. It is probably not in front of you, sir, but --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It should be on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go to page 8, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Toward the middle of where it says UK 3, the sentence begins: "I, Dusanko Grubor ..." In the middle, it says: "We went down there to the centre where we were supposed to go where Jovo Opacic registered us. We were supposed to come down today on Friday, to register and to go there with you. I don't know where you're taking us." Did you ever found out who Jovo Opacic was?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And was it your impression that you were supposed to take these people somewhere?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When she says, "you," she means UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well the transcript says, "to go there with you", it doesn't say "UNPROFOR."

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But when an old sort of peasant lady sees a white vehicle, she doesn't distinguish between UN TV and the UN humanitarian assistance or all the different branches.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And if you go to page 9, again at UK 3, the woman answers: "Jovo Grubor, he lives in Opacici. He came two days ago. He wrote down how many of us there were and told us to come on Friday, that UNPROFOR will come here, that they would take us, and that they would tell us when they would leave with us." Now, that's the second name we've heard for this person? Jovo Grubor, have you ever heard of Jovo Grubor?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- no, I hadn't heard of him before that. I remember when editing the piece, we said something like, I mean with the translators in Zagreb, I said, "Who would that be? Who is Jovo Grubor?" The village is called Grubor, so we just kind of assumed that maybe it was like a village elder.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And this particular person answers that: "UNPROFOR ..." --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this particular answer in the transcript says: "UNPROFOR will come here," but it says nothing about the mayor of Knin or any other Croatian official. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And if we go to page 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In the middle of the page, again, UK 3, the person was asked: "What are you go to do now?" And the answer is: "Well, we're not going to do anything. Jovo told to us come there, that you would chase us to Knin, to a camp. While there," and then it is unclear, "what we'll do -- we don't know what we'll do ..." --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. I can't find where you -- where is this again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sure. Page 10?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. In the middle, it says UK 3: "Well, we're not ..."

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just letting the translation catch up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It says: "Jovo told us again ..." -- Sorry. I will re-ask the question. Again it says: "Jovo told us to come there, that you would chase us to Knin, to a camp." Do you have any idea what the person means by that statement?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean right now, this second?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can only imagine. She was very confused in general and distraught. So whether some authorities, UN or Serbs or Croatians, had sort of said that, "We're going to get you out of here," you know, might have been the Croatian saying, "You've got to leave here." I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You're just guessing at that, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. Yeah. I have know idea. It was very confusing to listen to her, so that is all I can think of right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It was your impression, after speaking with her and with other people, that they were supposed to leave the area, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. No. I -- when we arrived -- you mean before or after this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: When you got there, on the 25th?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: When you spoke to these people?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You seem to have differing accounts from different people about what was going on, right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So there was some confusion?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Some people thought that UNPROFOR had called the meeting?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Some people thought that there was a Croatian official who had called the meeting?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody really knew anything?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And all these people showed up and nobody knows why?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, showed up where?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In that first meeting that you were at?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They didn't show exactly up because -- well, they were in the village. The village was just four or five houses, as far as I remember. So, yeah, they just showed up and then nothing happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Then you went and saw --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. My case manager has a huge sign here that says "slow down," and I'm not watching it, so I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: When you saw the flames or the smoke across the valley, you were still in that small village. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That small area --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And then you went back down?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And that was another area where there was a large of group of people. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. If you imagine, along a road, down along a road, base -- let's call it base village. And what I mean by that, it was the village near Grubori. Grubori is another kilometre, half a kilometre up the hill in the mountain. So it may have been -- that may have been Grubor village as well. It was down flat. It was a school area. There were people gathered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you didn't stop there though, right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: On the way back?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the way up, we stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sorry. On the way up, we did not stop. When we came down after seeing the burning houses, we did stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, when you went up to the houses that they were going to try to see where the smoke was coming from, you said there was a short clip that showed the path that you had to take to get up there. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It is safe to say, in order to get up there, you need a four-wheel drive vehicle?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Especially in the weather that you were dealing with for the day?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, that was very heavily wooded?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily wood, but it was sort of a hill. It was hilly, it was steep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Hilly, lots of trees?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Fairly rough terrain?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's terrain in which it would be pretty easy to hide?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Terrain in which there could be enemy armed combatants and you wouldn't know it unless you stepped right into it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's go up to where the burning -- or the smoke was coming from. You said, on the way up to the -- well, you tell me, where did you see the vehicles to your right, the empty vehicles?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. So, if you imagine, you come down from the first village, you go along a road. Before we start going up again, there are a long vats in between road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. And you said in your statement that from your recollection at least as of today, there were six vehicles, roughly?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And they were mini-buses?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jeeps. It was I think jeeps and one sort of mini-van like with no windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Was that the same kind of van that you saw as you were leaving towards Split?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was, in fact, identical, that large windowless van and jeeps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to show you a video-clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: This is part of P28, Your Honours, and we can mark it separately. There is no conversation. It goes from 34 minutes 6 seconds to 3 minutes 19 second. We can tender it as a separate exhibit since it is such a short clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just as we pause for a moment to get that video started, Mr. Kuzmanovic was referring to 65 ter 3770 and the transcript there to. We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, that is P872; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: That is P872. However, we had created 65 ter 5464 as being a part of 65 ter 3770. But the transcript that was presented is identical to the one that is P872.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry. That was my confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So there is no need to seek further admission of that; it is in evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That was part of my confusion. Thanks for clarifying that, counsel. Why don't we go to the clip. Your Honour, may we show the clip?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Stop it for a second. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That white windowless van, that was the same van that you saw on the road from --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, vans like that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: -- when you were going to Split --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- about, you know, a lot of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Keep going.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would to tender that video, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: No objection, other than it is a portion of P28. Do we want that as a portion --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It is of no matter to me. We shortened it because it was part of a larger clip, and if we want to keep it as P28 and refert to it by the minutes that I refer to before, that is fine with me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now I'm a bit lost. You want it separate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I had wanted to tender it as a separate exhibit, Your Honour, simply because it was just a very short clip of the mini-van -- of the jeeps and mini-bus that he had discussed in his testimony, rather than put the whole tape again and find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It makes sense. I remember that it was earlier played as a short clip as well, but then part of a larger video.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, during Mr. Flynn's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you assign a number to this extract from what is already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D784, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D784 is admitted into evidence. And we now all know that it's, to some extent, a repetition of what we have seen in a larger video earlier. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Before I get to the spot where you go up to where the smoke was, sir, I'd like you to refer to your statement; page 4 -- page 6, paragraph 41. This is, again, where you discussed where "the convoy of white mini-buses passed us going the same direction, 20 vans all unmarked." Now, during your direct testimony, you talked about this being perhaps something that you were worried about them wanting to pull you over and you refer to as being a little overdramatic, did you not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, white mini-buses, you could not have seen that they were full of uniformed personnels since those mini-buses, which you said were the same as the white mini-bus here, had no windows?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was a mixture. It was a mixture of the vans and then the jeeps that can you see in to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let's refer back to your statement: "As we were travelling, a convoy of these white mini-buses full of uniformed personnel passed us going the same direction." You didn't say anything about jeeps, correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. You specifically said white mini-buses, correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the white mini-bus, you said was the same as the white mini-bus in the video that you saw?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, because there were also buses without windows -- I mean, with windows. Basically, just to clarify, there seemed to me that the vehicles we saw in general on those two days were jeeps, the ones like in the -- the ones notice footage; there were vans with windows; and there were sort of smaller than those vans we just saw, a type of what can only be described as a mini-bus, with windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And who they belonged to or what they were doing have you no include?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do, in the sense that they were emblems on the side of some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: But you don't -- you can't tell what you say they are today?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Croatian police emblem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you don't mention that at all in your statement in 2001. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we talking about the convoy that passed us?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, paragraph 41.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I don't recall saying that there was an emblem on the side of the vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, you say there were 20 vans all unmarked in paragraph 41, correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So there were no emblems at least as according to your statement?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember -- I can't remember is the answer. I mean, there may have been --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters apologies. We cannot follow at this speed. Please make pause between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I should take an emblem as a speed police. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I know I would get a lot of tickets if that was the case, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Just to finish that theme, your statement said that there were about 20 vans all unmarked. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's go back up to see where you were going to see where the smoke had come from. When you got up to where the smoke was going on, you did speak with some people, correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And at that point, you knew of no casualties of any kind, correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall how many homes were on fire?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were about six, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And as a matter of fact, I think in one of your transcripts?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And I'm going to again to refer it to it as a 65 ter, and I'm sure Mr. Margetts hopefully will help me out if it has already been marked as an exhibit. It's 65 ter 3769 which is part of the 92 ter submission, Your Honour; just the transcript and not the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes that was re-marked as 65 ter 5465, and is P873.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: P873, on the second page, at the very top, there's a question that says: "Tell me, how many houses were there in Grubori." And the answer is there: "There are about 20." And the question is: "About 20 all together, the whole of Grubori? And the answer is: "The whole of Grubori." And then again someone asks: "We heard earlier that there were 40. And the response is: "No, no. No, no." So from your recollection, there were six homes burning out of 20?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So it is fair to state at least that the whole village of Grubori was not in flames, if there were six homes burning out of 20?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. And, actually, there was a question asked later --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. Some had burned out. When you say on burning, I'm talking about seeing flames coming out of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: And there were other charred houses with window-frames that were charred that had been burning, obviously, to me, and it was -- there was -- it was heavy rain. So I assumed, from the time we saw the plumes of smoke to when we got there, some had -- some of the burning had died down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You can't tell me right now whether those homes that you saw that you said had not been burning but appeared to have been burned was done on that particular day or was it done earlier. You can't tell me that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I can, in the sense that they were smouldering. So if you see a sort of window-frame still smouldering, I presume that that had happened that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Later on in this statement, you were asked: "How many houses are on fire now." And the answer is: "How are we supposed to know?" Then another answer: "We don't know. Well, we must count them, you, us. We'll count them now." And then at the end of that page, it says: "Four that are burning up there." So, at least as of the transcript of this particular interview that was done that day, there were four burning homes?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right, at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: But it is fair to state that the whole of Grubori was not on fire. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is fair. But there another something that may be relevant. To this day, I don't know whether the village down below, where there was no burning, I still don't know whether that was counted as Grubor as well; but, certainly, in the hamlet. Well, I call it hamlet because, as I say, there were much fewer houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So, then, after you took this video of these people, you left for Knin. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We went back down the hill; we stopped at the larger homestead, village, by a school; and then we went back to Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In your interview of these ladies, there was no discussion of who was present when the fires began. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And there was no discussion of what --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on the interview. But I had asked her -- they had sort of -- what happened, it seemed to me, was they had all been told by someone to go down to the other village, to the main part. And when -- in the confusion, someone had told the women that, you know, "your husband's gone." And somehow she realized, maybe someone told her, that he hadn't gone. So that's why she was still there, was my understanding at the time. Plus, there was some other old ladies there who were simply too frail to leave their homes anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sure. You refer to this in paragraph 17 of your statement, and in the middle of that paragraph. This is the lady that you interviewed which we had gone over the transcript, Dusanko Grubor, who told that you the UN had convened a meeting in the village below. Then in that same paragraph : "After leaving Grubori, she noticed plumes of smoke back in the village, so she returned to see what had happened as she feared for her husband's safety. She told us, 'My husband and a friend's husband are too old and couldn't go to the meeting.' She said she couldn't find her husband now." Now, there was no discussion at least in your statement or in the interview of what she thought caused the smoke and the fire to begin with. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you came back, and on your way back to Knin, you had the video with you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the video was then sent by helicopter to Zagreb that same day?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember whether we kept it with us and sent the whole package after the interview with General Cermak, or whether I thought I should sent it -- just that portion of the burning villages immediately. However, given that the most violent images were taken the day -- the next day, the two corpses, I assume or I'm pretty certain that I would have waited till after the interview with General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you said in paragraph 25 that Mr. Flynn told you that there were two elderly male bodies found, one had its throat slit and the other one was shot in the back of the head. Now, this is information you got from Mr. Flynn?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether there was any investigation done by any police authority that demonstrated that one person had his throat slit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: At any time.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean UN or Croatian police?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Any police?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know, no. But I saw it next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you a medical forensic examiner?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know -- well, you first saw the body inside a building, correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And that's the body that was -- allegedly had its throat slit?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that where the person was killed?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the person was dragged into that spot from the outside?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So, as far as you know, the person who you claim you saw that had his throat slit was killed in that spot where he lay?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, in paragraph 37 of your statement, you state: "This second victim was in the hallway near the front entry of the house. This victim was laying on his front. It was obvious his throat had been slit. He appeared to have fallen down." So did you videotape this person?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that this person had been found some distance away from the home and had been dragged there and placed there by someone?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the old lady had said something about finding her husband near the cow, but I didn't know whether that was correct or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So you can't tell me for a fact whether this person had his throat slit. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what I saw, and it looked like he had his throat slit. I mean, there was a deep, dark line around here, and there was a pool of blood on the floor, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There was a pool of blood on the floor?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you go and check and see from where the body had been dragged?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't know -- I assumed at that moment when we were filming, that it had been done there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So you broadcast the fact that this person was someone who had his throat slit without really knowing for a fact that that had happened?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I knew it because I had seen it with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You haven't seen somebody slit the this gentleman's throat. You saw a dead body lying on the floor, and you assumed he had his throat slit.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't assume. I could physically see that his throat had been slashed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There was not one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, you gave as an estimate of thought 30 to 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm almost done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're almost down. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Flynn [sic], there was not one instance in Grubori where someone was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, if you'd addressed the witness by his own name, that would be preferable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That would be preferable, Your Honour, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lyntton, there was not one verified case of any elderly person being dragged out of their home in pyjamas and shot in front of their home in Grubori. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The pyjama reference is the man that was in his pyjamas in bed, and had been dragged onto the floor in the house that we filmed in the footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So people were not dragged out of homes in Grubori in their pyjamas and shot, correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not people, but at least one person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In the whole house, correct, not out of the house?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And how that happened you don't know either, correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: He was shot, he was dead, the circumstances of that you don't know?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You did not report any of this to the police in Knin, correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Croatian or UNCIVPOL?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Croatian?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the sense that I told General Cermak what we had found.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he is not the police, is he?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assumed he --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking to you assume. Was he -- General Cermak was not the civilian police in Knin, correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness finished his answer, what he assumed? What did you assume?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assumed that the man wearing a uniform just days after what had happened, the cleansing of Serb, would know -- I mean, whether he was police or military, that was the authority. There was no distinction for me coming outside -- coming from outside. They were the authorities. So I assume that the military person I was talking to would tell the police if that was their procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: My question to you was: You didn't tell the police, correct? You didn't tell the civilian police in Knin what you had seen, correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not because I didn't -- I as far as I knew, there was no police, so, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you never made an attempt to find out who the police person was supposed to be that was supposed to come to Grubor that day, correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Again, because in such a small area with so few people visible, to me, General Cermak was the one in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you sent a videotape out of what had happened without really discussing any details with the police or finding out what kind of investigation they were going to undertake or did undertake?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't have any other questions Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kuzmanovic. Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I probably have at least 15 to 20 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Lyntton, during the course of the cross-examination, particularly various questions that Ms. Higgins asked you, you were asked about your impressions of General Cermak's authority and what you based those impressions on. You were also asked about your impressions of General Cermak's knowledge of events in Grubori and what you based those impressions on, and you enumerated a number of factors. Now, you had the opportunity to speak with General Cermak at some length; and the interview which you conducted with him, we have and we've looked at today. Did the answers that he gave you to the various questions you asked give you any impression as to his authority?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Now, you have the transcript of the interview before you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I think you do. If I am not mistaken, I think that's the interview --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... that's on the same -- this is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... villages, if you look to your right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, this one, yeah. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I think now have you it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: That's P504. If I had more time, I may just ask you to consider the entire interview, but, instead, I think it is more efficient if I take to you various answers and then I ask you for your comment on those portions of the interview. The first part I'd like to take you to of P504, the English transcript, is on the first page. And you, after discussing the events in Grubori in the initial questions with General Cermak, you then asked specifically: "Could he give a description of the combat, the kind of combat that took place in the village." And you'll see that question just below the midway point of the first page. And he gives you some details about the number of members of the special police, what they were doing; and the final sentence of that answer he says: "And at that moment, when they were fired at, our special forces returned the fire; and, well, that returning of fire resulted in, well, wounding and it resulted in setting houses on fire." Now, we looked at that specific answer in your examination this morning. So I'm now asking about any of these things that I referred to that in any manner made an impression on you. I'd now like to take you to the bottom of page 2. And we also looked at this this morning, the issue of humanitarian assistance, and the last clarification that General Cermak seeks is he asks what village and what police forces are you talking about. You tell him Grubori. And then if we go over to page 3, General Cermak then gives an explanation if there were police cars and he refers to check-points. Then in the last part he says: "These were blocking points ..." This is the last three lines of the answer appears at the top of page 3: "These were blocking points. So the police had their basic task to wait for any of these members of the Chetnik formations or, well ..." --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Apologies. We just need to be mindful of the interpretation, so I will just pause for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: "... or, well, the Serbian military to show up at these blocking points." And he says: "This was their task and they were carrying out that task." Then you ask the next question, and you talk about the ten empty vehicles. Then he answers you as follows. He says: "Look, I don't know. He asked me today. The gentleman put the question to me today. He said, "Today I saw six police cars ... outside of this village. I wasn't there. I couldn't see that. I can only tell the gentleman one thing: 'Had we wanted to cover up anything, had we not wanted something to be known, we wouldn't have let them get close to that area.'"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, you're now reading for a couple of minutes sequences which we have heard earlier today. I take it at the end you would say what impression did it give you or kind of question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why not put a question to the witness at this moment, rather than to seek. Of course, Ms. Higgins has shown us where in the interview Mr. Cermak says, "I don't know." "I don't know." And, of course, there are other parts of the interview where he explains exactly what had happened. I mean, the Chamber can read, can listen, and, of course, the Chamber can think to the extent that where Ms. Higgins pointed at certain portions that this was not the whole of the interview. Now you are apparently completing the whole of the interview, so that we have heard it twice, and that we know what other people get as an impression on the basis of that; whereas, primarily, I think it is what impression or what conclusions the Chamber could draw from that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It is just out of an abundance of caution I wish to provide a full -- I mean, as I said, I would like him to be able to read the whole interview. I will just refer to, then, two sentences without giving the entire previous context.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: In the middle of the page, General Cermak says: "I will gather all the information, I will get a full report from the civilian police, from the special police, and then we can get together again and talk about this whole case again." And then further down on that same page, General Cermak says: "If anything illegal occurred, I will personally carry out an investigation." Now, as you understand, everyone has the transcript before them, you conducted the interview, you have had an opportunity to read that interview. And my question is simply that: In terms of your impression, and that was the impression you conveyed in your evidence today, the impression conveyed in your witness statement that he was the military governor in charge of the area, in terms of what he said to you in interview, did you gain an impression of his level of authority in the area?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. He seemed to know what was going on, and the fact that he was offering to investigate what I had told him, again, led me to -- to think that, you know, he has some considerable influence, command, and knowledge of what is going on here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Now, one of the questions you were asked by Ms. Higgins was whether you had the opportunity to question whether General Cermak was the so-called military governor. At any stage, was there any information conveyed to you by anyone whilst in Knin or, alternatively, during the course of the interview with General Cermak that would have caused you to question your impression as to his authority?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Ms. Higgins also asked you -- she said, after you had relayed some of the detail that you knew about the events in Grubori, she asked you didn't it, in fact -- didn't it become, in fact, clear that during the course of that interview and given his responses, he didn't actually know at that time the extent of what had happened up there; and you said no. And she asked would you that be fair, and you said not exactly. Now, what was your impression in that interview, in light of the information that you possessed and had gathered in your two visits to Grubori and in the manner in which General Cermak had answered the various questions from the start of the interview? What was your impression as to his knowledge and his denial?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interview, for me, could be spread into three parts. The first bit was a confident commander, answering about his general knowledge of the area. Then, when I started getting specific, I felt that he began to get a little bit flustered, the body language, the eyes battering. So, as a journalist, I thought I was on to something. And then third part of the interview, when I went into the specifics, I felt that he was becoming very sort of polite and speeded up the process, sort of wanting to finish. And it just didn't gel for me; the tone, how he started, didn't stay consistent throughout the whole interview. So I guess could you say, in other words, I didn't totally believe him, and I wanted -- that's why I kept pressing certain questions, to see what reaction they might provoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one final matter, and that was when you were in Grubori and actually filming the burning homes. Did you walk around the village in any attempt to survey the entirety of the village, or did you seek merely to capture the footage that we've seen?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did. We walked around as much as we could. We obviously wanted the dramatic fire shots. That was the crucial thing. So, once we got those, we wanted to get out, because Flynn and the interpreter were very, very worried, I mean, that someone might find us there --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and do something nasty to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And do you feel that you informed yourself as to which homes had been on fire and been extinguished --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: -- or which homes had been --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: -- damaged? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Margetts. Ms. Higgins.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I just have several questions arising from the questioning of my learned friend Mr. Kuzmanovic and my learned friend Mr. Margetts, if Your Honour would permit me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please put those questions. May I invite the parties - of course, I'm not directly addressing you, although you appear to be the one to put further questions to the witness - to seek facts rather than impressions, because a lot of things that appear to be rather obvious when looking at the video and, Mr. Margetts, in the totality of the account, of course no one would have expected Mr. Lyntton to go through the village closing his eyes for the smoke and start counting houses and then to interview people on how many people lived in those houses. Of course, that is so obvious, isn't it? It rather becomes a -- let's try to avoid that this becomes a bad tradition, and Ms. Higgins will now be the first one to show that it is not. Please proceed.
