utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Just a few additional questions. You've already -- I have already dealt with you about the remit of your actual knowledge of Mr. Cermak's authority, given the limited time you were in the region.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I'm not going to deal with that again. You've given me answers on that. In respect of the interview that you had with Mr. Cermak, you have also confirmed to me, have you not, that did not know and were not told where he got his information from. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Thank you. I think, having locked at the transcript in some detail now, you would also agree with me that in the transcript of the interview, you called him General but you never called him military governor. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, you referred, when asked by my learned friend Mr. Kuzmanovic about the purpose of the UN film, and you mentioned propaganda and that there was a certain story that you were asked to look for. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: To use your words, you described it, in terms of the footage and story about Grubori, as a perfect story. And to be fair to you, as an UN producer and director, you had what you called the evidence, and you had what you called a denial. And, so, technically, you had a good classic format for a film. Would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: It's right, however, isn't it, that in the film that you made about Grubori, you didn't include in that footage the seven occasions that I have shown to you about Mr. Cermak saying the words, "I don't know." Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Yeah. Thank you very much, Mr. Lyntton.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Higgins.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually, sorry. Can I just add something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean, that last question, he does -- one of the key sentences was, I don't know where the gentleman got his information from that people were taken out and put in their pyjamas, et cetera, that I did include in my piece. So he does say, "I don't know where," to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That furthers the position of your answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one question for you. You earlier were asked where we find in the transcript that those two elderly people told you about people in Croatian uniform arriving and with Croatian emblems. Now, you answered the question by saying, no, that does not appear in the footage in the transcript. Did they tell you, so even if not recorded, did they tell you that people had arrived Croatian uniforms with Croatian emblems?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: They told me "Ustasha," "Ustasha." They kept using that word. They said it was Croatian military. This is in the preamble, you know, when we first met them. And I cannot remember whether I said specifically, "Was there a Croatian police emblem on their sleeve?" But my practice in those cases was always to try and ask that question, but I honestly just can't remember whether I specifically asked those two people that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, whether they mentioned Croatian uniforms or confirmed that and Croatian emblems or confirmed that, you do not have sufficient recollection anymore to --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the word "uniform"; but "Croatian," that was clear that it was Croatian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By the way, you referred to police emblems are always gained the impression that it was not specifically about police but, rather, military, as you also said. Was that a slip of the tongue?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I said what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just find it for you. Yes you said: "And I cannot remember whether I said specifically was there a Croatian police emblem on their sleeves; whereas, for me, the whole context was military rather than police."

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that a slip of the tongue?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. Also, at the time, we all often intermingle those two words, police, military, police military. They were so intertwined for us working in that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that answer. One final point to verify: What you produced, you said it was broadcasted by other television stations. Was it produced in any way as a commercial production?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. It was just that you were employed, it was made available or was it sold to these --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, no, no. The films, in general, were for consumption by Serb, Croatian, and Bosnia local TV stations, which, of course, were free; and even when the footage that was given -- the raw footage was given to the networks, no, that was not commercial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. May I take it that the questions by the Bench have not triggered any further need. Then, Mr. Lyntton, this concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming and for answering the questions that put to you by the parties and by the Bench. I wish you safe journey home again. And for the parties, we'll adjourn and we resume on Wednesday, the 17th of September, at 9.00 in the morning, in this same courtroom, III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 17th day of September, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.
